ciphertext_pointer: ciphers/pollaky-1865-1875/ciphertext.txt (single pass, draft, 25 Sept 2026, worker bPOL); images in ciphers/pollaky-1865-1875/images/ with manifest.json; full numbers in ciphers/pollaky-1865-1875/NOTES.md. alphabet: unknown per ad: ad 1 invented symbols ('secret script'); ad 2 digits ('number code'); ads 3-4 undetermined until transcribed

constraints.source: Tony Gaffney's 'The Agony Column' (as Jean Palmer) catalogues twelve Pollaky-signed ads; these four are the ones Schmeh received scans for and that remain unsolved ('there are two more encrypted Pollaky ads that might have been solved by Thomas Ernst; I won't cover them here' -- Schmeh)
constraints.biographical_context: Bryan Kesselman (Pollaky's biographer) read and transcribed several hundred surviving Pollaky letters in UK and US archives (National Archives Kew, Hertfordshire Archives, Hartley Library Southampton, Sanford Museum FL); none give a clue to his ciphers, and 'Pollaky seems to have used several different ciphers, but none of the ciphertexts seems to be long enough to decipher it'
constraints.expected_difficulty: short texts, multiple distinct systems across the four ads, no key material found in the biographical archive search to date

cheap_tests_in_order: 1. Fetch the four images (one host, scienceblogs.de, 1.5-2s apart) and run a blind transcription pass on each, recording letter/symbol/digit counts and distinct-symbol counts per ad; without a transcription no cryptanalytic test is possible. Cost $2, Sonnet.

2. (Restated 25 Sept 2026 by LANE B2 for NEAR.md row pollaky-1865-1875.) Ads 3-4 are the Evening Standard 8 and 20 May 1875 ads of ciphers/catokwacopa-1875 (partial: the line-pairing mechanism is agreed in print by Bosbach, Estes, Ernst; unique plaintext not reconstructable), so no substitution or columnar family is run on them here. Instead: a second blind transcription pass of ads 3-4 from images already on disk, reconcile with tools/reconcile_passes.py, then diff the reconciled text line by line against the transcription in Bourdeau's cyphersolver (catokwacopa ads.py, from Thomas Ernst's BNA-checked text; MIT, cite, clone shallow and delete) after normalising case and punctuation (rule 3). Report pass agreement and the target-vs-Bourdeau letter agreement side by side; every disagreement to a TSV with image crop. This is an independent image-based check of the text the catokwacopa target rests on (its LOCAL-QUEUE L13 gap), not a solve. Cost $4, Sonnet. (Earlier wording, kept: 2. Once transcribed, check ad 2 (the 'number code' ad, 1871-02-20) against contemporary telegraph/commercial codebooks the way Lima-1916's cheap test 1 did (tools/print_check.py-style grep against Internet Archive djvu.txt of period codebooks -- ABC Code, Western Union, Lieber's), since a Victorian ...)

3. Cross-check ads 3-4 against Gaffney's 'The Agony Column' text (if a full-text copy can be located, e.g. Internet Archive or Google Books) for any partial reading Gaffney himself may have proposed but that Schmeh's post did not reproduce. Cost $1-2.
